question: Does avoiding temporal expansion help when action/outcome histories are enormous, and which known reductions explain any advantage?
renewal_exact: Separate verified specialized control: activate all free nonnegative renewable items; pointwise dominance proves optimality without a temporal tree. Rejected for the coupled shared-market family.
variants: Public known probabilities cycle through 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75; both inventories receive the same seeded permutation; private environment/planner seeds are separate.
uncapped: Initial-observation complete local controls at size 8; exact full-horizon search only at size 2 and 2 rounds; no unlimited intractable search is claimed complete.
ci: 95% percentile bootstrap of whole paired blocks, 4000 resamples; exploratory, unadjusted comparisons on synthetic cases.
history_counts: Exact unmerged action/outcome history counts for renewable families only, NOT distinct states, executed operations, or savings credited to HS. The shared-resource family does not use a stationary branching-power claim.
timing: C policy boundary, excludes parsing, Python and actual environment transitions. Soft time caps can overrun.
memory: Owned heap separately from stack and process RSS; RSS covers both agents and launcher high-water effects.
preservation: Every outcome, decision, configuration, seed, source version and failure is retained; previous tournaments and Derrisor unchanged. Timing pilot is separate from the predeclared tournament.
